newsitem.title: USA: AFTER THE BELL - Quiet trading after record day.
newsitem.headline: AFTER THE BELL - Quiet trading after record day.

text.p: Traders saw limited after-hours trading activity on Friday, after a buying frenzy earlier in the day pushed the Dow Jones industrials to a record high.
"We're real quiet. It seems as if everybody's gone home," one trader said.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average jumped 66.58 to 5838.52 in very heavy trading Friday.
In late corporate news, retailer 50-Off Stores Inc said it was considering filing bankrupcty or selling the company due to deteriorating results.
Glenayre Technologies Inc and Anadigics Inc also issued cautionary statements about their third quarter results.
Traders, however, said they saw no activity in these stocks.
The New York Stock Exchange said 43,000 shares were traded in the first after hours session, compared to 2,500 shares Thursday.
In the second session, 8,111,600 shares changed hands. No shares were traded in session two on Thursday, the exchange said.
The American Stock Exchange reported no after hours trading activity.
